subject: Post-demo: Knowledge grounding & retrieval tuning for VelaHealth
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@velahealth.com>, Samir Mehta <samir.mehta@velahealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Knowledge grounding & retrieval tuning for VelaHealth

Hi Aisha / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of where we landed (very high level):
- Goal: Reduce hallucination in clinical advice snippets while keeping latency < 400ms P50 for caregiver search flows.
- Current Vela baseline: 85% grounding coverage on FAQ set; hallucination complaints mostly on multi-paragraph synthesis.

Redwood recommendations for first-pass eval (what we can ship quickly):
1) Retrieval stack: hybrid sparse+dense (BM25 on clinical index + dense ANN using text-embedding-3-small).
2) Reranker: CrossEncoder-MiniLM (fine-tune on 500 labeled QA pairs) — prioritizes grounding precision@5.
3) Model for generation: start with open Llama-3-8B-q4f then compare against Redwood-verified gpt-like baselines (we'll produce cost/latency table).
4) Metrics to capture: grounding_precision@K (K=1,5), grounding_coverage, hallucination_rate (binary label), answer_fidelity_score (human-rated 1-5).

Deliverables we proposed on the call:
- Redwood will share a small benchmark pack (sample prompts, 120 eval queries, and a scoring rubric) by EOD today.
- Vela shares a redacted sample of 2k search logs + 400 gold QA pairs (PII-safe) so we can run the first pass evaluation.

Concrete next steps / asks from Vela:
- Can you confirm who on your side will share the logs and sample labels? (Samir / ML team?)
- Any constraints on bringing the sample data into our private evaluation environment (VPC vs. S3 link)?

I'll attach the demo recording and the benchmark skeleton. If this schedule looks good we'll queue a short config workshop (30m) to lock retrieval parameters and reranker training plan.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Knowledge grounding & retrieval tuning for VelaHealth

Thanks Hannah — this is great and aligns with what Aisha and I discussed. A few clarifying Qs from the ML side: 

1) For the hybrid retrieval, do you recommend we use our current clinical BM25 index (with medical token filters) + Redwood's dense index, or should we reindex into a single pipeline on your side for the evaluation?
2) For the reranker, is CrossEncoder-MiniLM an out-of-the-box model from your catalog or would that be a Redwood fine-tune? How much labeled data do you expect to meaningfully improve NDCG-ish measures?
3) About metrics: can you share the exact rubric for 'hallucination_rate' (binary vs graded)? Our compliance folks prefer a conservative binary definition but product wants nuance.

We can share a redacted S3 link; I'll coordinate with infra but expect a delivery by next Tue (2026-08-04).

Samir
Lead ML Engineer — VelaHealth
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Mehta <samir.mehta@velahealth.com>, Dr. Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@velahealth.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Knowledge grounding & retrieval tuning for VelaHealth

Hi Samir — short answers and one proposal for the workshop: 

1) Hybrid index: For the first eval it’s simplest if Vela keeps your BM25 clinical index and we spin up a read-only dense index on our side using the same doc ids. That avoids reindexing effort and keeps parity with your production tokenization. If we see a large delta we can propose a consolidated reindex later.

2) Reranker: CrossEncoder-MiniLM is in the Redwood catalog as a starting point (no initial fine-tune). For material improvement on reranker NDCG and grounding_precision@5 we recommend 300-800 labeled pairs; performance gains taper after ~1k. We can run active learning to prioritize labels.

3) Hallucination rubric: we attach the rubric (binary + graded fallback). Short version: primary label = grounded (0/1). Secondary tags capture partial factuality, overgeneralization, and unsupported inference (1-3). We'll send the full rubric in the benchmark pack.

Workshop proposal (30–45m):
- Attendees: Samir, 1× engineer who owns search infra, Aisha (product lead), Hannah, Marissa, Diego
- Agenda: confirm S3 access method, map doc ids between systems, set retrieval recall targets, define the 500-pair reranker labeling plan, decide canary evaluation thresholds
- Proposed times: Thu 2026-07-30 09:00-09:45 PT or Fri 2026-07-31 11:00-11:45 PT. Tell me what works.

If you confirm S3 share, we'll provision a dedicated RBW evaluation job and post results in a shared Drive link.

Thanks — Hannah

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Knowledge grounding & retrieval tuning for VelaHealth

Great thread — quick technical add from my side on reranker + eval metrics: 

- Reranker choice: if latency budget is tight consider a two-stage approach: sparse-first (BM25) -> fast bi-encoder re-ranker (DistilBERT dot-prod) to get top-50 -> Cross-Encoder-MiniLM only on top-10. This keeps P95 latency low while improving grounding_precision@1.
- Retrieval params we plan to sweep in the eval: dense vector dim (384 vs 768), ANN recall target (0.95 vs 0.99), BM25 k1 (1.2 vs 1.6), and passage windowing (single doc vs sliding 200-token windows).
- Proposed grounding metric set (short): grounding_precision@1, grounding_precision@5, grounding_coverage, factuality_score (3-pt manual), and regression_alert if hallucination_rate increases by >3 percentage points vs baseline.

I uploaded a starter prompt set and an example labeled pair schema to the Drive link Hannah included. Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-demo-eval-Vela (same as above). Also attaching a tiny CSV we use to track labeler agreement.

If you want, Diego and I can run a 60-min workshop to walk through the reranker training flow and labeling UI after you share the S3 link.

—
